pretreatments.description: Organosolv pretreatment using aqueous ethanol, 50% (v/v), with catalysts including H2SO4, HCl, CH3COOH, or NaOH; solid to liquid ratio 1:10; heated at 190°C for 15, 30, 45, or 60 min; followed by washing with 50% aqueous ethanol and distilled water until pH 7; dried at 60°C; solid fractions used.

Hydrothermal pretreatment using distilled water, heated at 190°C for 15, 30, 45, or 60 min; solid to liquid ratio 1:1; followed by washing with distilled water until pH 7.0; dried at 60°C; solid fractions used.

Combined organosolv and hydrothermal pretreatment: Napier grass pretreated with organosolv, then combined hydrolysate and solid fraction mixture of organosolv-pretreated grass used as substrate; Napier silage pretreated with organosolv, then combined hydrolysate and solid fraction mixture of organosolv-pretreated silage used as substrate.

Combined organosolv and hydrothermal pretreatment: Napier grass pretreated with organosolv, then combined hydrolysate and solid fraction mixture of hydrothermally-pretreated grass used as substrate; Napier silage pretreated with hydrothermal, then combined hydrolysate and solid fraction mixture of hydrothermally-pretreated silage used as substrate.
Enzymatic hydrolysis using Cellic® CTec2 (20 FPU/g-substrate) with 50 mM sodium citrate buffer at pH 5.0 at 50°C for 72 h.

Anaerobic batch digestion in 120 mL serum bottles with 20 g VS/L of anaerobic sludge as inoculum; substrate at designated amount with or without added 29 mL enzymatic hydrolysate and solid fraction mixture; purged with nitrogen gas; incubated at 150 rpm; methane content analyzed via gas chromatography.
Biogas volume measurement using wetted glass syringe method; methane analysis via gas chromatography.
Solid yield calculation based on dry weight after pretreatment divided by dry weight before pretreatment; lignin removal and hemicellulose removal calculation.

Cellulose, hemicellulose, and lignin content analysis according to NREL/TP-510-42618; TS and VS determination using APHA standard methods; morphological and compositional analysis via SEM and XRD; sugar concentration via HPLC; biogas composition via GC.

Preparation of anaerobic sludge inoculum from SF Khon Kaen Co., Ltd. biogas plant; enrichment in 6 L bottles with 4 L sludge and 10 g Napier silage; incubation at room temperature for 3 weeks; separation of non-degradable materials by filtration through 10-mesh screen.
Enrichment of anaerobic sludge for methane production; collection from biogas plant co-digestion of Napier silage with chicken manure; storage at room temperature.
